releases.displayName: Motor Vehicle Accident Expansion & free Shannondale Update out now!

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45535639/53edcab3177168f3bc77d5748b86e3cf5bed8fc1.png"]
Oakridge City just got bigger, busier, and more dangerous.

The Motor Vehicle Accident Expansion is now available for Firefighting Simulator: Ignite, introducing a new type of emergency response to your shifts. For the first time, you can take on complex vehicle accident sites, rescue trapped civilians, manage new hazards, and use specialized rescue tools to bring the situation under control.
Watch the Motor Vehicle Accident Expansion Release Trailer here:

At the same time, the free Shannondale Update is now live for all players, opening the freeways and adding a brand-new district to Oakridge City. From airport emergencies to industrial incidents and new side missions, Shannondale brings fresh challenges to every crew.

notes.title: Your new emergency response: Motor Vehicle Accidents

items.text: The Oakridge City FD firefighters have completed their advanced training course, and vehicle accident calls are now part of the job.

In the Motor Vehicle Accident Expansion, you’ll arrive at accident scenes where every decision matters. Assess the scene, extinguish fires, contain dangerous leaks, and rescue civilians trapped inside vehicles.

Use the hydraulic rescue tool to pry open car doors and work through heavily damaged vehicles. When obstacles block your path, grab the rescue chainsaw and cut your way through. With new mechanics such as vehicle extrication, sawing, and leak plugging, these missions add a new layer of hands-on rescue gameplay to Firefighting Simulator: Ignite.
Included in the Motor Vehicle Accident Expansion
Five new main missions
New side missions
New gameplay features and emergency response mechanics
New tools, including the hydraulic rescue tool and rescue chainsaw
Vehicle Extrication, sawing, and leak-plugging gameplay
New accident-site hazards to manage
This is the biggest addition to Firefighting Simulator: Ignite yet, expanding your range of emergency calls and giving you new ways to work under pressure.

Whether you’re responding to a massive fire at the airport flight school, handling a private jet incident during refueling, or getting a first look at the motor vehicle accident gameplay in the free sneak peek mission, Shannondale adds more variety to your shifts from the moment you roll out.

notes.title: New DLC: Motor Vehicle Accident Expansion

items.text: Accept the call and handle motor vehicle accidents with the Motor Vehicle Accident Expansion for Firefighting Simulator: Ignite – adding new missions, new gameplay mechanics, new tools, and more.

The Oakridge City FD Firefighters have completed their advanced training course and are now also able to manage vehicle accident sites. The Motor Vehicle Accident Expansion adds five additional main missions as well as more side missions to your experience. Firefighting Simulator: Ignite's biggest expansion also adds several new gameplay mechanics and techniques, including vehicle extrication, sawing, and plugging leaks to prevent further spillage.
The MVA Expansion includes five brand new main missions as well as five new side missions (which appear randomly).

Welcome to Oakridge City’s new and growing district Shannondale, known for the Oakridge City Regional Airport and its ever-expanding industrial areas. items.text: The Vehicle Customization Update is now available for free on all platforms.
While poking around the apparatus bay, we stumbled upon a few forgotten paint buckets and spare parts. Naturally, we put them to good use and just like that, vehicle customization is officially here!

Visit the apparatus bay to customize all your vehicles with individual color schemes, sirens, and light patterns. All vehicles come with a variety of preset color patterns for you to choose from, but of course you can create and store your own custom patterns. You can also customize the vehicle’s siren sounds by choosing between individual options for the wail and yelp. Lastly the emergency lights section allows you to select a new custom pattern for the emergency lights of each vehicle. Each vehicle can be customized individually and presets can be stored and shared between them.
Owners of the Blackout Truck Edition Skins DLC (to be released tomorrow) will also have access to additional coloring options.
\ Separate inputs for emergency lights and siren (wail) – they can now be toggled independently.
\ Several graphical issues

\ Fixed an issue that could lead to multiple mission markers appearing on the minimap

items.text: Grab your gear and get ready – The Alarm Mode Update is here to shake up your routine in Oakridge City! The sirens are blaring, the calls are coming in, and it’s up to you to respond when duty calls.

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45535639/57f5dfda6ed186cda939a21d0b835417290d1f1a.png"]
With this update, we’re introducing a major new feature: Alarm mode.

Experience dynamic mission alarms at random interval while in the fire station – no two shifts will ever be the same. Customize and fine-tune your alert frequency and preferences to match your playstyle. Choose whether you want to progress your career or replay completed missions — it’s entirely up to you.

notes.title: 🏠 Back at the station: relax, prepare, and suit up.

items.text: Between alarms, the fire station is now more alive than ever!

In the previous update, we added station wear — so now you can kick back and take off your heavy gear while off-duty. You’ll also find new ways to interact with your surroundings: explore the station, discover fun little details, and enjoy some downtime before the next alarm sounds.
If you haven’t checked it out yet, this is the perfect time to explore everything the station has to offer!
🔥 Full Changelog – Alarm Mode Update
New Feature: Alarm Mode
Dynamic mission alarms at random intervals
Choose between career focus or replaying completed missions
See the Map Menu or the settings (Gameplay > Experience) for preferences
New Feature: Single player pause
Optionally pause the gameplay when in a menu (single player only)
Find this setting under Gameplay > Interface
Improvements: AI Autonomy
Added separate autonomy settings to define the AI squad's priority roles while acting autonomous
Prioritizes victim rescue before extinguishing fires
Prioritizes extinguishing fires before rescuing victims
Mixed: Assigns different roles to the available AI squad, with the first and third member prioritizing extinguishing, and the second member prioritizing victim rescue
“Search & Explore” task removed, integrated its functionality into “Search & Rescue”
While checking rooms for potential victims, the AI squad will also interact with discovered breaker boxes and gas valves
Improved AI aiming when extinguishing fire
Changelog
Added alarm lights to the training area and training building
Fixed some issues with achievements/trophies not unlocking correctly
Fixed some issues with DLCs not unlocking when the game fails to connect to the servers
Fixed some issues with in-game statistics for clients
Fixed an issue where completed approaches didn’t count for the client drivers
Fixed some camera clipping issues
Fixed an issue where dangerous goods couldn’t be pinged
Fixed an issue where the ping on breakable walls wasn’t centered
Fixed an issue where the network disconnected message was shown in single player games
Visual improvements for bloom from vehicle lights, fire, etc.
Enabled shadows for bridges
Improved road network so vehicles cause less traffic jams
Improved blending of road meshes with the landscape
Fixed tool getting stuck to the belt when on a ladder while a mission is started
Fixed some settings not enabling immediately when a related setting changes
Fixed map interaction in mission room available, even though it can’t be used during the tutorial
Fixed image on the Thermal View tool flipped when looking at it in first person
Fixed menu buttons sometimes stuck in blocked state after cancelling quick play search
Fixed several localization issues
Several performance and stability improvements

🔥 Hotfix #3 is live! 🔥
We just released our third hotfix for Firefighting Simulator: Ignite!
Hotfix #3 addresses some issues that got reported by players during the last weeks. Here’s the full list of fixes and improvements:
Fixed some issues related to player progression when alternating between Multiplayer & Singleplayer
Fixed an issue when joining a multiplayer game via invitation
Reduced the frequency of some voice lines
Improved general game stability
Thanks for all your feedback and reports and helping us to make Firefighting Simulator: Ignite the best it can be! 🔥
Your Firefighting Simulator team
The fire never sleeps — and neither do we!
Hot on the heels of our first update, Hotfix #2 has rushed to the scene to tackle even more issues you’ve reported.
This update includes several fixes and improvements to keep your firefighting experience running smoothly.
Fixed several translation issues
Fixed crash when joining the same multiplayer lobby more then once
Improved AI Firetruck Navigation
Fixed an issue in the vehicle selection for Mission "Just Tuning The Engine"
Fixed an issue in the Mission "Stuck at the Office" which prevent some areas from being extinguished
Improved general game stability
Thank you for all your feedback and reports — you’re helping us make Firefighting Simulator: Ignite the best it can be!
Stay safe out there,
Your Firefighting Simulator Team 🧑‍🚒

The call has come in, and it’s time to answer. Camp Woodchuck, Oakridge’s historic summer retreat and beloved local tradition since 1921, is under threat from a fast-spreading fire.
Jump into action with Firefighting Simulator: Ignite – Summer Camp DLC, now available! Gear up, strategize, and tackle these brand-new missions to save the heart of Oakridge.

In addition to the new DLC we just released our first big update for Firefighting Simulator: Ignite. Next to a ton of bug fixes and general game improvements this update also introduces the option to change your gear as well as a number of smaller and funny things to do within the fire station. We wish you a good time exploring!
New Feature: Station Gear

Next to some other additions to the fire station, you're now free to change your clothes between turnout and station gear. By default, this is done automatically based on the situation (mission and training area vs. any other time), but the behavior can be adjusted in the settings.
New DLC: Summer Camp
We’ve released our first mission DLC, Summer Camp. Head to the store to check out Camp Woodchuck.
